Subject: Post-incident update: FastFin throughput/latency — root cause & mitigations applied

Raj / FastFin ops — thanks for your patience. Final summary and customer-facing points below.

What happened (short):
- Between 08:48–09:30 PDT a combination of an autoscaler controller race and an unintended cache eviction regression increased backend load on a subset of serving shards. That pushed p95/p99 up and generated transient 502s for the affected shard set.

What we did:
- Immediate: applied a temporary routing policy at 10:10 to move ~40% of traffic to stable model variants (reduced error rate within minutes).
- Medium: rolled a canary hotfix for the autoscaler and reverted the cache eviction change by 12:45; canary metrics showed normalized latencies.
- Telemetry: delivered logs bundle and SLO slices (links attached).

Current status:
- Latency and 502s have returned to baseline across all regions as of 17:20 PDT.
- We're monitoring for 48h and will surface any regressions immediately.

Next steps / ask of FastFin:
- No action required today. If you see anomalies please escalate via this thread.
- We'll share a customer-facing root cause analysis and postmortem by 2027-03-21 COB.

Attachments included: fastfin-prod-logs.tar.gz, slo-telemetry-snippet.txt, throughput-qps.csv

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
